html: CAUSAL FEEDBACK FROM A COUNTABLE FAMILY OF COMPLETE PROFILES Private ASTRA-FRESH-20261023 / P1. 23 October 2026 UTC. A separate exact interface. All earlier proofs remain unchanged. 1. THE POINT OF THE RESULT An open-loop record bound in L2 of a common reference measure can be lifted to causal feedback when the realized complete command-and-sensor schedule belongs to a countable family. The price is an explicitly charged selection complexity, not the size of the hidden physical field or number of sensor visits. This supplies a restricted feedback extension of the moving-sensor Gaussian-overlap theorem. It does not supply arbitrary continuous-valued feedback, or justify treating a random schedule as independent of its record. 2. CANONICAL CAUSAL CONTRACT There are two hidden models, indexed by v=0,1. In either model construct the experiment under a common reference Wiener record law W on [0,T]. The primitive hidden noises and hidden initial preparation are independent of that reference record, conditional on any declared public data and coins. The same actual predictable policy is used in both models. Conditional on a complete reference record y, it fixes a deterministic public profile u[y]. That profile includes every commanded physical coefficient, the complete observation gain/probe schedule, and any public response prehistory required by the hidden transition law. The two models retain their own hidden noises. Assume the standard measurable, well-posed conditional reference construction: given y, each hidden law is the law obtained with the deterministic profile u[y]. The physical record is obtained by its normalized causal likelihood. For the Gaussian observation, bounded total gain energy and bounded signal ensure normalization. More generally this argument only needs the stated conditional-kernel and normalized-likelihood properties. Fix a finite or countably infinite collection of COMPLETE deterministic profiles {u_j : j in J}, each admissible in both models. Let rho_v^j(y) be the physical record density for the open-loop experiment u_j relative to W. Suppose the actual causal policy has a measurable index I(y) with u[y]=u_(I(y)) for W-almost every y. (2.1) Equality includes the complete sensor and physical-control functions up to the equivalence required by the stochastic construction. Put E_j={y:I(y)=j}, p_j=W(E_j), d_j=||rho_0^j-rho_1^j||_(L2(W)). Discard W-null E_j. These events partition the reference record space. Crucially, I is not asserted independent of y or of either physical hidden state. Its selection is the actual feedback policy. Causality is required for the policy to define the normalized physical experiments in the first place; an arbitrary future-dependent selection need not do so. 3. DENSITY SELECTION IDENTITY The adaptive physical record densities obey rho_v^ad(y)=rho_v^(I(y))(y) W-a.s. (3.1) Proof. Condition the reference construction on the complete record y. On E_j, its physical commands, sensor functions, public responses, and initial context coincide with the deterministic profile u_j. Its conditional hidden path law and its likelihood functional therefore coincide with those in the open-loop experiment u_j evaluated at y. Integrating that likelihood over the conditional hidden path proves (3.1). No independence between the selector and record, no posterior restart, and no hidden-state coupling is used. In particular the selected density pieces are not renormalized within their branch events. 4. SELECTION INEQUALITY With TV defined as one half the L1 difference of record densities, TV(P_0^ad,P_1^ad) =1/2 sum_j int_(E_j)|rho_0^j-rho_1^j|dW <=1/2 sum_j sqrt(p_j) d_j <=1/2 (sum_j d_j^2)^(1/2). (4.1) The last inequality uses sum_j p_j=1 and is useful when its right side is finite. The first inequality can be better when branch masses are unequal. Both may always be capped by one. Countable sums follow by monotone convergence; a divergent displayed bound is simply uninformative. In particular, if d_j<=Delta uniformly and C_sel=sum_j sqrt(p_j)<infinity, then TV(P_0^ad,P_1^ad)<=min{1,Delta C_sel/2}. (4.2) For at most M profiles, C_sel<=sqrt(M), so TV(P_0^ad,P_1^ad)<=min{1,sqrt(M)Delta/2}. (4.3) Equivalently C_sel=exp(H_(1/2)(p)/2), with H_(1/2)(p) the order-one-half Renyi entropy of the PROFILE INDEX UNDER REFERENCE WIENER MEASURE. This is an exact mathematical size of the selected family, not the physical mutual information acquired about the hidden system, not a controller running-time bound, and not automatically a quantity cheaply computable from the policy. If independent public coins choose a family or policy, condition on those coins first. Average the resulting conditional TV bounds. An unbounded independent randomization over open-loop schedules incurs no selection factor merely for having many coin outcomes. The charge concerns dependence on the measured record. All initial-law and admissibility conditions must hold after the same conditioning. 5. MOVING-SENSOR APPLICATION For the controlled copying-spin field, suppose each deterministic complete profile admits the common degree-D polynomial endpoint certificate E_D(n,T) and the exact common regional JOINT initial law. The target polynomial semigroups preserve degree and contract allele coefficient l1 norm. Every profile may use an arbitrary measurable deterministic moving probe phi_t(x)=sum_a w_a(t)x_a, with sum_a|w_a(t)|<=1, and deterministic real gain H_t with int_0^T H_t^2dt<=Gamma. The sensor may visit arbitrarily many regions or switch arbitrarily often. Common physical controls and their causal responses are deterministic within this open-loop profile. The Gaussian-overlap argument gives the uniform open-loop L2 allowance Delta_n^2 <= sum_(d>=1) [(9Gamma)^d/d!] d^2 E_d(n,T)^2. (5.1) Indeed a product of d signal observables has temporal coefficient norm at most 3^d. The all-state temporal telescope costs at most d E_d(n,T), using the nondecreasing-in-interval-length envelope. The exact Gaussian mixture L2 identity integrates the SQUARE of the difference of these d-time moments with factor product H(t_i)^2 and 1/d!. The integrated weight is Gamma^d. For the held regional theorem E_d(n,T) is a polynomial of degree at most four in d, with coefficients O(n^(-1/2)) at fixed physical budgets. Thus the series in (5.1) is finite and O(n^(-1)). This assertion uses the exact polynomial certificate, rather than only pointwise-in-degree convergence. Consequently a causal policy with at most M admissible complete profiles satisfies TV(P_micro^ad,P_field^ad) <= min{1, (sqrt(M)/2) [sum_(d>=1) (9Gamma)^d d^2 E_d(n,T)^2/d!]^(1/2)}. (5.2) The error is uniform in every finite number of regions, even when that number grows with n. The observation energy, horizon, internal mixing and activity constants, and cross-region rate envelope remain fixed. If M=M_n grows while M_n/n->0, the estimate still tends to zero. No uncharged growth of the physical budgets is admitted by that statement. 6. AN ACTUAL CAUSAL CONTROL CLASS Fix r deterministic decision times. At each time, the policy uses the full observed record so far to choose one of at most b predeclared continuation segments. For every possible finite sequence of choices, the concatenated complete physical and sensor profile is deterministic and admissible. Every complete profile must satisfy the common energy and physical bounds. Then the family has at most b^r members and (5.2) applies with M=b^r. Decision rules may be arbitrary measurable functions of the past record; they need not be continuous or Lipschitz. A segment may sweep arbitrarily many sensor locations. For fixed b>=2 and budgets, r<= (1-epsilon)log_b(n) with any fixed epsilon>0 gives the displayed sufficient vanishing condition. This is a conservative sufficient allowance, not an optimal feedback depth. Random continuous switching times, continuously valued gains chosen from the record, or arbitrary function-valued feedback usually create an uncountable family of complete profiles. They are NOT included merely by calling their commands bounded. The fixed-bank theorem separately permits far more general feedback, using a different proof. Neither theorem contains the other in all experimental directions. 7. INTERPRETATION AND OPEN INTERFACE The effective physical field and public response memory are unchanged. The extension concerns which interventions its predictions survive. Two distinct complexities appear: a field may have arbitrarily many coordinates and a sensor may visit arbitrarily many of them, while the record-dependent choice among complete physical schedules is still charged by (4.1). This selection inequality is a sufficient transfer bound, not a lower bound or an assertion that arbitrary feedback must pay sqrt(M). Its growth might be removable by an adapted residual theorem or stochastic observable norm. The reference-energy bound alone does not justify deleting it, and the held conditional-norm counterexample does not prove that it is necessary. For genuinely unrestricted moving-sensor feedback, the outstanding interface is a causal averaged comparison that controls the record-dependent profile without taking a worst hidden state after seeing future reference noise. This source provides a complete restricted construction rather than that missing general estimate. Novelty, optimality, practical numerical advantage, and extensions to quantum measurement remain UNKNOWN. END OF SOURCE

CAUSAL FEEDBACK FROM A COUNTABLE FAMILY OF COMPLETE PROFILES

Private ASTRA-FRESH-20261023 / P1. 23 October 2026 UTC.
A separate exact interface. All earlier proofs remain unchanged.

An open-loop record bound in L2 of a common reference measure can be lifted
to causal feedback when the realized complete command-and-sensor schedule
belongs to a countable family. The price is an explicitly charged selection
complexity, not the size of the hidden physical field or number of sensor
visits. This supplies a restricted feedback extension of the moving-sensor
Gaussian-overlap theorem. It does not supply arbitrary continuous-valued
feedback, or justify treating a random schedule as independent of its record.

2. CANONICAL CAUSAL CONTRACT

There are two hidden models, indexed by v=0,1. In either model construct the
experiment under a common reference Wiener record law W on [0,T]. The
primitive hidden noises and hidden initial preparation are independent of
that reference record, conditional on any declared public data and coins.
The same actual predictable policy is used in both models. Conditional on
a complete reference record y, it fixes a deterministic public profile u[y].
That profile includes every commanded physical coefficient, the complete
observation gain/probe schedule, and any public response prehistory required
by the hidden transition law. The two models retain their own hidden noises.

Assume the standard measurable, well-posed conditional reference construction:
given y, each hidden law is the law obtained with the deterministic profile
u[y]. The physical record is obtained by its normalized causal likelihood.
For the Gaussian observation, bounded total gain energy and bounded signal
ensure normalization. More generally this argument only needs the stated
conditional-kernel and normalized-likelihood properties.

Fix a finite or countably infinite collection of COMPLETE deterministic
profiles {u_j : j in J}, each admissible in both models. Let rho_v^j(y) be
the physical record density for the open-loop experiment u_j relative to W.
Suppose the actual causal policy has a measurable index I(y) with

                    u[y]=u_(I(y)) for W-almost every y.        (2.1)

Equality includes the complete sensor and physical-control functions up to
the equivalence required by the stochastic construction. Put

 E_j={y:I(y)=j},  p_j=W(E_j),
 d_j=||rho_0^j-rho_1^j||_(L2(W)).

Discard W-null E_j. These events partition the reference record space.
Crucially, I is not asserted independent of y or of either physical hidden
state. Its selection is the actual feedback policy. Causality is required
for the policy to define the normalized physical experiments in the first
place; an arbitrary future-dependent selection need not do so.

3. DENSITY SELECTION IDENTITY

The adaptive physical record densities obey

                 rho_v^ad(y)=rho_v^(I(y))(y) W-a.s.           (3.1)

Proof. Condition the reference construction on the complete record y. On
E_j, its physical commands, sensor functions, public responses, and initial
context coincide with the deterministic profile u_j. Its conditional hidden
path law and its likelihood functional therefore coincide with those in the
open-loop experiment u_j evaluated at y. Integrating that likelihood over
the conditional hidden path proves (3.1). No independence between the
selector and record, no posterior restart, and no hidden-state coupling is
used. In particular the selected density pieces are not renormalized within
their branch events.

4. SELECTION INEQUALITY

With TV defined as one half the L1 difference of record densities,

 TV(P_0^ad,P_1^ad)
  =1/2 sum_j int_(E_j)|rho_0^j-rho_1^j|dW
  <=1/2 sum_j sqrt(p_j) d_j
  <=1/2 (sum_j d_j^2)^(1/2).                                (4.1)

The last inequality uses sum_j p_j=1 and is useful when its right side is
finite. The first inequality can be better when branch masses are unequal.
Both may always be capped by one. Countable sums follow by monotone
convergence; a divergent displayed bound is simply uninformative.

In particular, if d_j<=Delta uniformly and

                  C_sel=sum_j sqrt(p_j)<infinity,

then

           TV(P_0^ad,P_1^ad)<=min{1,Delta C_sel/2}.           (4.2)

              TV(P_0^ad,P_1^ad)<=min{1,sqrt(M)Delta/2}.       (4.3)

Equivalently C_sel=exp(H_(1/2)(p)/2), with H_(1/2)(p) the order-one-half
Renyi entropy of the PROFILE INDEX UNDER REFERENCE WIENER MEASURE. This is
an exact mathematical size of the selected family, not the physical mutual
information acquired about the hidden system, not a controller running-time
bound, and not automatically a quantity cheaply computable from the policy.

If independent public coins choose a family or policy, condition on those
coins first. Average the resulting conditional TV bounds. An unbounded
independent randomization over open-loop schedules incurs no selection
factor merely for having many coin outcomes. The charge concerns dependence
on the measured record. All initial-law and admissibility conditions must
hold after the same conditioning.

5. MOVING-SENSOR APPLICATION

For the controlled copying-spin field, suppose each deterministic complete
profile admits the common degree-D polynomial endpoint certificate E_D(n,T)
and the exact common regional JOINT initial law. The target polynomial
semigroups preserve degree and contract allele coefficient l1 norm.

Every profile may use an arbitrary measurable deterministic moving probe
phi_t(x)=sum_a w_a(t)x_a, with sum_a|w_a(t)|<=1, and deterministic real gain
H_t with int_0^T H_t^2dt<=Gamma. The sensor may visit arbitrarily many
regions or switch arbitrarily often. Common physical controls and their
causal responses are deterministic within this open-loop profile.

The Gaussian-overlap argument gives the uniform open-loop L2 allowance

 Delta_n^2 <= sum_(d>=1) [(9Gamma)^d/d!] d^2 E_d(n,T)^2.      (5.1)

with factor product H(t_i)^2 and 1/d!. The integrated weight is Gamma^d.

four in d, with coefficients O(n^(-1/2)) at fixed physical budgets. Thus
the series in (5.1) is finite and O(n^(-1)). This assertion uses the exact
polynomial certificate, rather than only pointwise-in-degree convergence.

satisfies

 TV(P_micro^ad,P_field^ad)
  <= min{1, (sqrt(M)/2)
       [sum_(d>=1) (9Gamma)^d d^2 E_d(n,T)^2/d!]^(1/2)}.      (5.2)

The error is uniform in every finite number of regions, even when that
number grows with n. The observation energy, horizon, internal mixing and
activity constants, and cross-region rate envelope remain fixed. If M=M_n
grows while M_n/n->0, the estimate still tends to zero. No uncharged growth
of the physical budgets is admitted by that statement.

6. AN ACTUAL CAUSAL CONTROL CLASS

Fix r deterministic decision times. At each time, the policy uses the full
observed record so far to choose one of at most b predeclared continuation
segments. For every possible finite sequence of choices, the concatenated
complete physical and sensor profile is deterministic and admissible. Every
complete profile must satisfy the common energy and physical bounds. Then
the family has at most b^r members and (5.2) applies with M=b^r.

Decision rules may be arbitrary measurable functions of the past record;
they need not be continuous or Lipschitz. A segment may sweep arbitrarily
many sensor locations. For fixed b>=2 and budgets, r<= (1-epsilon)log_b(n)
with any fixed epsilon>0 gives the displayed sufficient vanishing condition.
This is a conservative sufficient allowance, not an optimal feedback depth.

Random continuous switching times, continuously valued gains chosen from
the record, or arbitrary function-valued feedback usually create an
uncountable family of complete profiles. They are NOT included merely by
calling their commands bounded. The fixed-bank theorem separately permits
far more general feedback, using a different proof. Neither theorem contains
the other in all experimental directions.

7. INTERPRETATION AND OPEN INTERFACE

The effective physical field and public response memory are unchanged. The
extension concerns which interventions its predictions survive. Two distinct
complexities appear: a field may have arbitrarily many coordinates and a
sensor may visit arbitrarily many of them, while the record-dependent choice
among complete physical schedules is still charged by (4.1).

This selection inequality is a sufficient transfer bound, not a lower bound
or an assertion that arbitrary feedback must pay sqrt(M). Its growth might
be removable by an adapted residual theorem or stochastic observable norm.
The reference-energy bound alone does not justify deleting it, and the held
conditional-norm counterexample does not prove that it is necessary.

For genuinely unrestricted moving-sensor feedback, the outstanding interface
is a causal averaged comparison that controls the record-dependent profile
without taking a worst hidden state after seeing future reference noise.
This source provides a complete restricted construction rather than that
missing general estimate. Novelty, optimality, practical numerical advantage,
and extensions to quantum measurement remain UNKNOWN.

END OF SOURCE
